opening_message:
Ticket 1: Alexandra Johnson (employee ID E003) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E003.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Alexandra Johnson (E003) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Source Code. As full-time staff, max is write unless role owns the system; Source Code is owned by Engineer, so admin is not permitted. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E003 (Alexandra Johnson) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors can have read, or write with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin exceeds max, so grant read.
reason: Requested admin access to Source Code. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, and E003's role is Analyst, so admin is not permitted regardless. The notes conflict on employment type (HR: full_time, max write; Security: contractor with basic training, max read). Granting read is within policy under either interpretation, and since admin exceeds the maximum, I grant the conservative maximum of read.
